taxonomyNote: NatureServe uses a narrow sense of L. californiae that excludes L. nigrita (Krysko et al. 2017); NPS Death Valley lists it as Lampropeltis getula californiae.
fieldMarks: Highly variable pattern: black and white or brown and cream, with bands or longitudinal stripes; aberrant animals may show dots, zippers or bars (NPS Cabrillo).
Usually 2.5-3.5 ft, up to about 4 ft (NPS Cabrillo); NatureServe gives typically 76-107 cm.
behavior: Constrictor that eats small mammals, lizards, amphibians, birds, large invertebrates and other snakes (NPS Cabrillo).
Resistant to rattlesnake venom and known to eat rattlesnakes (CDFW).
Inactive periods are spent in crevices or burrows, or under rocks, logs, stumps or other cover (NatureServe).
habitat: Primarily terrestrial; forest, woodland, shrubland, swamps, marshes, river bottoms, grassland, semidesert, desert and farmland (NatureServe).
range: Southern Oregon, western and southern Nevada, southern Utah and extreme southwestern Colorado south through California and Arizona to southern Baja California and northern Sinaloa (NatureServe).
